notes: Written against script.md (script a, picked 2026-10-05) and take1@1.08.words.json, which narration.json names. B1's Display drops the spoken '방이' so the frame-0 chunk fits 4 eojeol (see Captions below).

Geometry is px in the 1080×1920 frame, origin top-left; points are [x, y]. A Hotel is placed by origin (room 1's left wall x, the floor line y) and room [w, h]; room n's center x is origin.x + (n − 0.5) w, its roof is floor − h.

One hotel, three layouts. Big (B1, B2, and B7's end, the loop): origin (264, 845), room 120 × 200 (roof y 645), fade x 624 → 936, ground from x 160; room centers 324, 444, 564, 684, 804, 924 (rooms 1–3 full, 4 at 0.81, 5 at 0.42, 6 at 0.04); the newcomer at the door stands at x 204. B3 (two hotels, room for room): both rooms 62 × 130 from x 152, the 10-room hotel's floor at 670 (roof 540), the infinite one's at 950 (roof 820, fade 834 → 936); room n's center 121 + 62n, so room 10 is at 741, the end wall at x 772, and right under the wall and the pushed-out guest (803) sits the infinite hotel's room 11 (803, full opacity), then 12 (865, 0.70) and 13 (927, 0.09). B4: origin (152, 788), room 90 × 160 (roof 628), fade 692 → 936; centers 107 + 90n (197, 287, … 737 at 0.82, 827 at 0.45, 917 at 0.08), so 1→2, 2→4, 3→6 and 4→8 are all on screen; the newcomers' street line stands 230 px below the floor (feet y 1018, tags to y 1070).

Why three sizes: frame 0 wants the hotel as big as it can be while still reading as endless (5 rooms before the fade at w 120); B3 needs 13 room widths across 792 px (w 62, the writer's ~12 widths), with room 10 against the wall over the infinite hotel's room 11 as the focus (the critics' preference); B4 needs room 8 on screen for 4→8 (w 90). The door spot exists only in the big layout; B3 and B4 put room 1 at the left edge (x 152), so the picture stays centered without it.

Rows (B5–B6): two NumberRows on B4's room centers (x 197 + 90 (n − 1)) with B4's fade: the top row, 1, 2, 3, … (the rooms the guests came from), at B4's room-number height (ink center y 668), so it is the room numbers themselves; the bottom row, 2, 4, 6, … (the rooms they moved to), at y 856; TeX 58 px (digits 46.7 px tall, '10' 61.6 px wide, 28 px apart at the 90 px step). Pairing lines: vertical, x 197 + 90 (n − 1), y 704–820, 12 px clear of both rows' ink. Row names centered on the frame: '자연수' ink center (540, 595), 24 px above the top row; '짝수' (540, 929), 24 px below the bottom row.

Frame 0 is the hook: the big hotel, visibleAtStart, full (a blue guest in every room out to the fade), its numbers 1–6, and the yellow newcomer standing at the door left of room 1, under the first caption '무한한 호텔이 꽉 찼어요.'. The ink spans x 160 to about 911 (where the fade drops under the ink level), y 643–847: the full width of the zone at its middle. A row of rooms is long and low by nature; taller rooms would only add empty space above the guests, and wider ones would show fewer rooms before the fade.

Endless means fading: an infinite hotel, its arrows and the number rows are drawn at full opacity left of the fade's start and fade linearly to 0 at x 936, the content edge minus 4 px (004's bounds lesson: the encoder spreads an edge a few px). Nothing is drawn past x 936: the fade is applied per drawn piece (each segment or glyph at the opacity of its x, so the probe sees it) and clipped at x 936, since a piece near the end can straddle it (the bottom row's '18' at x 917 is 62 px wide; its teal at 0.08 still counts as ink).

Loop: the last frame is the first. Both show the hotel in the big layout, a blue guest in every room, numbers, walls and ground at full opacity, no light, and the yellow newcomer at the door; nothing else is alive. B7 turns the newcomers in the odd rooms blue (they are guests now) as a new newcomer stands at the door. The last caption ends at the pause (until), so the loop's last frames carry none and frame 0's caption follows.

Honest moves (research C15, C17). Every move is all guests at once: they start together, slide straight along the floor and land together. In 2n the row of guests stretches to twice its spacing (guest n is always at n times the current spacing), so no one walks ahead or arrives after another; the arrows say who goes where, which is the mathematics (the assignment). Newcomers move straight along their own arrows into their rooms, also all at once. In B3, the 10-room hotel's empty room 1 is never lit, and nobody is admitted to it: the picture shows only that this one move pushes someone out (C17).

Color meanings hold for the whole episode: a guest's color says who it is (blue: was already in the hotel; yellow: new), and an arrow takes the color of the guest it moves. B2's newcomer turns blue on B4's first word, when the hotel recenters, so the 2n move is only blue guests and yellow keeps meaning 'new'. Yellow also lights an empty room: a room for a newcomer.
Draw order is declaration order: inf < hops < fin < finHops < dbl < qArrows < rowN < rowE < lblN < lblE. Arrows draw over the hotel; the rows draw over the fading hotel.

An element is invisible until its appear cue, unless it has visibleAtStart. Cues sharing an anchor run in parallel, except that an appear waits for the exits on its anchor. Every exit is a 0.2 s even fade. Easing from theme.ts: ease.out for appear, ease.exit for exit, ease.smooth for everything else, unless params say ease: linear or cruise. A beat's first-word cue that isn't an entrance or exit is linear (B2's pulse) or cruise (B3's move), so it shows within the 3-frame reaction window. B1, B6 and B7 have no cue on their first word.

Numbers never move from one element to the other by being drawn twice: when the top row appears (B5) it takes over the hotel's room numbers on that frame (the hotel stops drawing them), and when it gathers back (B7) the hotel draws them again from the frame the row lands. The bottom row's copies leave the even rooms' numbers under 0.3 opacity until clear of them. Check-render fails any two texts meeting, moving or not.

Text: in the visual zone, only TeX numbers and the two row names. Room numbers and the newcomers' tags are TeX 44 px (digits 35.5 px tall; '10' 46.7 px wide, which leaves 5.6 px to each wall in B3's 62 px rooms); the rows TeX 58 px; '자연수' and '짝수' in Note (Pretendard SemiBold 56, advance width 145 and 97 px). Captions measured from Pretendard-Bold.otf advance widths at 60 px: widest '짝수는 자연수의 일부인데도요.' 719 px, then '수학에서는 이렇게 짝지어지면' 702 px and '2배인 방으로 옮기면 돼요.' 614 px; all fit one 800 px line.

Extents worked out from the geometry, not yet measured on a render: the 2n arcs in B4 that rise from fading rooms (n = 6–8) reach about y 400 near x 936, where they are nearly gone; the tallest clearly visible one, 5→10, peaks at y 453; the B3 hops clear the end wall by 21 px; the guests at w 62 clear each wall by 8 px; the pulsed row numbers (1.2×) clear the pairing lines by 5.5 px. B5's arc-to-line straightening and the bottom row's flight cross the top row's numbers while moving (a warn at most); if it reads badly, the lines may grow in place as the arcs fade.

components.name: Hotel
components.spec: A hotel seen from the front: one row of numbered rooms, each holding at most one guest, and newcomers waiting outside. Props: rooms (a count N: rooms 1..N, ending in a wall; or 'infinite'); origin [x, y] (room 1's left wall and the floor line); room [w, h]; fade [x0, x1] (infinite only: the hotel is drawn at opacity 1 left of x0, falling linearly to 0 at x1, nothing past x1; per piece, so the probe sees it); ground (x where the floor line starts on the left); guests {color} (every room full from the start); waiting {at: door, color} (one newcomer at the door: one room width left of room 1's center, on the floor). Drawing: room outlines muted, 4 px (stroke.line), neighbours sharing walls, the roof one line along the tops, no fill; the floor line muted 4 px from `ground` into the fade (a finite hotel's to 0.6 w past its outside spot); a finite hotel's end wall after room N in text, 6 px (stroke.sheet), floor to roof. Room numbers: TeX 44 px in text, ink centered on the room's center x at roof + 40; they never scale. A guest is a person icon centered on its room, standing on the floor, scaled with w: a body 0.6 w wide and 0.55 w tall with its top corners rounded at 0.2 w (shoulders), a round head of radius 0.16 w centered 0.75 w above the floor, filled in its color at 0.6 with a 4 px outline in its color (0.91 w tall: 109 px at w 120, 82 at 90, 56 at 62). A lit room (empty, for a newcomer): outline yellow 4 px over the walls, fill yellow at 0.15. Street line: newcomer k stands under room k's center, feet 230 px below the floor, its tag k (TeX 44 px, in its color) centered under its feet, ink top 16 px below them. A finite hotel's outside spot: one room width right of room N's center, on the floor. Exposes its live geometry (rooms, roof, floor, number places, street and outside spots, fade) to RoomArrows and NumberRow. Actions: appear (fade in); exit; moveTo {origin, room, fade, ground} (geometry only: strokes and number size never scale; guests stay in their rooms); pulse {part: guests | rooms | numbers | wall | waiting, rooms?: [n]} (guests: fill 0.6 → 0.85, outline 4 → 6 px and back; rooms: those rooms' walls muted → text and back; numbers: scale 1.2 and back; wall: 6 → 10 px and back); with wave: true, a rooms pulse runs left to right through every room into the fade over its span, so the eye follows the row off the edge; shift {map: n+1 | 2n} (every guest in a room moves at once from room n to room map(n), sliding straight along the floor; all start and land together, so in 2n the row stretches to twice its spacing; in a finite hotel a guest whose new room is past N slides through the end wall to the outside spot); light {rooms: [n] | odd} (lit at once, out to the fade; a light goes off when a guest lands in its room); lineUp {at: street, count: infinite, tags: true, color} (the street line appears newcomer by newcomer from the left into the fade over the span) or {at: door, color} (one newcomer fades in at the door); admit {map: 1 | 2k-1} (the waiting newcomers move into rooms at once: the one at the door slides right into room 1; street newcomer k moves straight along its arrow up into room 2k−1, its tag fading as it leaves; all land together and become those rooms' guests in their color); setGuests {rooms: all | odd | even | outside | [n], color?, opacity?} (recolor or fade guests; a guest at opacity 0 still holds its room); setStyle {rooms?, ground?} (those parts' opacity). Its room numbers are handed to a NumberRow and back (see NumberRow).

components.name: RoomArrows
components.spec: Arrows showing an assignment between places in a Hotel, read from its live geometry and fade. Props: of (a Hotel id), from: rooms | street, map: n+1 | 2n (from rooms) or 2k-1 (from street), color. From rooms: one arrow per room n, a half-ellipse above the roof from 6 px above room n's roof at its center + 0.15 w to 6 px above room map(n)'s roof at its center − 0.15 w, its height 0.4 × that span, 5 px (stroke.arrow), its 18 px head (mark.head) at the tip pointing down into the target room. In a finite hotel, room N's arrow arcs over the end wall and points down at the outside spot (the room that isn't there). From street: newcomer k's arrow is straight, from 14 px above its head to 8 px below room 2k−1's floor at its center. Arrows run on into the fade, every point at the hotel's opacity for its x; curves are polylines (geometry.ts). Actions: appear (all at once, each growing from its tail); exit; setStyle {which?: [n], opacity?, color?}; pulse {which?} (stroke 5 → 8 px, head 1.3×, and back); pairTo {top, bottom} (2n only: each arrow n straightens into a plain vertical 5 px line at NumberRow top's n-th x, from 12 px below that row's ink to 12 px above NumberRow bottom's n-th number, its head shrinking away; from then on it follows those rows and their fade).

components.name: NumberRow
components.spec: A row of numbers going on to the right. Props: values: n | 2n (the n-th number, n = 1, 2, 3, …), x0 (the first number's center), step, y (ink center), size (TeX px; 58 = type.mathInline), color, fade [x0, x1] (as Hotel's). Actions: appear {from: hotel} (all at once, each number starts on the hotel's room number of the same value, at its size and place, and moves and grows to its own place; a row of n takes over the hotel's room numbers: from the cue's frame the hotel no longer draws them, so no number is drawn twice; a row of 2n starts as copies of the even rooms' numbers that fade in as they leave, under 0.3 opacity until clear of the number they left; a number whose room lies past the hotel's fade fades in at its place); pulse {which?: all | even | odd} (scale 1.2 and back); setStyle {which: all | even | odd, color?, opacity?}; gather {into: hotel} (a row of n only, the reverse: each number moves and shrinks onto room n's number in that hotel's live geometry, taking its color; the hotel draws its numbers again from the frame they land, and the row is no longer drawn; each number's opacity follows the fade at its x, the row's at the start and the hotel's at the end); exit.

components.name: Note
components.spec: One line of plain text with $...$ math (studio/src/components/Note.tsx): props text, at [x, y] (the ink center), color (default text); type.label. Actions: appear, exit, setText. Used for the row names '자연수' and '짝수'.

beats.name: 한 칸씩

cues.note: '있어요': the answer is about the newcomer. Linear so it shows within 3 frames
'모두 동시에': every guest at the same moment, out into the fade

cues.note: '방이 열 개뿐인': the infinite hotel shrinks and moves down (rooms 62 × 130, roof y 820, floor y 950, fade 834 → 936), its dimmed arrows with it. Cruise so it shows within 3 frames

'똑같이': the same arrows, all at once; room 10's goes over the wall to nothing

beats.name: 두 배 번호

cues.note: '새 손님이': the 10-room hotel goes

'끝없이 줄지어': the newcomers line up on the street in front of the hotel, one under each room, from the door side on into the fade, each with its number tag 1, 2, 3, …

beats.name: 크기가 같다
